exposure: Hour of breastfeeding initiation within 24 hours postnatally
cohort: 3315 infants born at a university center and followed to age ≥12 months at 27 university primary care clinics
finding: Delaying breastfeeding initiation to >1 to ≤24 hours after birth is not associated with decreased breastfeeding duration compared with initiating breastfeeding at ≤1 hour after birth.
mod_finding: Delaying breastfeeding initiation to >1 to ≤24 h after birth is not associated with decreased breastfeeding duration compared with initiating breastfeeding at ≤1 h after birth for infants born via vaginal or cesarean delivery.
